title: Equivariant module presheaves and sheaves for an internal group action
statement: Fix compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $C$ be a small category, let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $C$ as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $K:C^{op}\to\mathrm{Grp}$ be a presheaf of groups with values in the coefficient universe. For a presheaf of unital rings $A$ and a presheaf of $A$-modules $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a restriction-natural linear $K$-action consists of monoid homomorphisms $K(U)\to\operatorname{End}_{A(U)}(M(U))$ such that $f^*(a\cdot m)=(f^*a)\cdot f^*m$ for every $f:V\to U$, $a\in K(U)$ and $m\in M(U)$. Define the category of equivariant $A$-module presheaves to have these pairs $(M,\mathrm{action})$ as objects and the restriction-natural sectionwise linear maps commuting with every group action as morphisms. Identities and composition are those of the underlying module presheaves, and addition is sectionwise addition of linear maps. For a sheaf of unital rings $R$ on $(C,J)$, define $\mathcal E_K(R)$ to be the full subcategory whose underlying $R$-module presheaf is a sheaf. Its preadditive structure is inherited from equivariant module presheaves. The forgetful functors to module presheaves and to module sheaves retain every underlying module and map; the inclusion of equivariant sheaves in equivariant presheaves does likewise. When a commutative ring sheaf $S$ is given, its underlying ring sheaf is obtained by composing with the forgetful functor from commutative rings to rings. In particular these definitions apply when $K$ is a group sheaf.
